office: Apostle of the Seventy, Bishop of Colophon

feast.note: The source itself calls this day the second memory of the company: its life of them closes «Все эти апостолы мирно преставились к Богу (вторая память 30 марта)». The first is not named on any page read here, and the 30 марта day page is the page that prints him, so that is the day this row keeps. The Ohrid Prologue, which this folder already cites, records 30 March as a separate day for two of the seven, and the Russian calendar prints five of them on it.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Σωσθένης, Κηφάς, Απολλώς, Τυχικός, Καίσαρ και Επαφρόδιτος οι Απόστολοι εκ των Εβδομήκοντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry names all six of its members and gives each his own couplet and his own paragraph, so it is one folder per named member and each relates the others. The page quotes Chrysostom as reckoning this Sosthenes and the Crispus of 4 December to be one person — «Oίμαι δε τούτον και Σωσθένη λέγεσθαι» — and the author ruled on 3 October 2026 that they are (TODO item 13 row 10), so the 4 December row below is the second half of this record. The identification remains Chrysostom’s, reported by the page and settled by neither page; it stands in the life as that. The corpus keeps a `sosthenes-of-chalcedon`, a soldier martyr of the Russian 16 September, who is another entry and another man. The page prints one hymn, an apolytikion that names Tychicus, so it is his and not this man's. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Κρίσπος»

attestations.note: The second Greek day, kept as «Άγιος Κρίσπος». Its page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους» and carries two hedged claims, both kept as hedges in the life: that he is «λέγεται» the founder of the church of Aegina, and that according to Chrysostom he is the apostle Sosthenes, quoted from the thirty-ninth homily on the Acts. It adds the one thing that points the same way without Chrysostom: **some hagiologies keep Crispus on 8 Δεκεμβρίου with others of the Seventy, Sosthenes among them**, which is a synaxarists’ day and not one saint.gr itself keeps. No asterisk, no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, no hymn, no distich and no year. The corpus’s `sosthenes-of-chalcedon`, a soldier martyr of the Russian 16 September, is another man and nothing joins him here.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.12.2025 (8. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети апостоли Состен, Аполос, Тихик, Епафродит, Онисифор, Кифа и Кесар.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, AN ENUMERATED COMPANY OF SEVEN NAMES, so BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 counts seven and each of the seven folders takes this one heading whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. The corpus holds all seven, so there is no arrival here. He is the first name. ONE NAME MORE THAN THE GREEK LINE: saint.gr’s 8 Δεκεμβρίου prints six — «Άγιοι Σωσθένης, Κηφάς, Απολλώς, Τυχικός, Καίσαρ και Επαφρόδιτος» — and this book adds Онисифор, who already stands venerated on another Serbian day and takes a note instead of a row. `types` UNTOUCHED: «апостоли» is the `apostle` held and `bishop` is the see this entry itself gives him. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND STILL ABSENT: the entry gives no year and no century for any of the seven. THE BOOK DISAGREES WITH THIS FOLDER’S OWN DISPLAY NAME: «Свети Состен би епископ у Кесарији» — he was bishop in CAESAREA, where this corpus calls him Sosthenes of Colophon and gives the Caesarea to `apollos-the-apostle`. NOTHING WAS RENAMED and the disagreement is recorded here and in the life. THE BOOK’S OWN OTHER DAYS, recorded and not acted on: all seven are celebrated on 4 January with the rest of the lesser apostles; it gives separate days to Apollos (10 September), Onesiphorus (7 September) and Cephas and Caesar (30 March). This row records the day whose heading it quotes. NO `related` ROW ADDED: the five other men of the Greek six are already `related` here in both directions, and Онисифор is not — sharing a heading is not a relation, which is BRIEF-SERBIAN §6, so the life does not name him. NO `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
